claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with Alex and are you responsible for their day-to-day care (such as feeding, clothing, and providing for their general welfare)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me, but I do contribute towards their upkeep - I help out with money for their needs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

**Who does Alex live with, and what is your relationship to that person?** (For example, does Alex live with their other parent, a grandparent, or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent - my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand a bit more about the financial support you provide.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep per week, and is this arrangement formal (such as through the Child Maintenance Service) or informal?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep - things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing. It's an informal arrangement between me and my ex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Does your ex-partner (the parent Alex lives with) currently receive Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they don't currently claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask one more important question to complete my assessment.

**Are you and Alex both currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK - I'm here in England and Alex is too, just with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: To qualify for Child Benefit, you must be "responsible for the child," which means you need to live with the child and be responsible for their day-to-day care (such as feeding, clothing, and looking after their general welfare).

Since Alex lives with their other parent and not with you, you don't meet this requirement. While you do contribute £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, financial contributions alone are not sufficient to qualify as being "responsible for the child" under Child Benefit rules.

**Important:** Your ex-partner, who lives with Alex and provides their day-to-day care, would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. They should consider making a claim if they haven't already done so.
